summary.title: Fixing Technical Debt with an Engineering Allocation Framework
summary.one_liner: You learn a bucket-based framework (Functional Improvements, Program Work, Delivery Performance, Unplanned Work) for classifying technical debt and allocating engineering time so debt gets fixed without stopping feature work.
keywords: how to fix tech debt without stopping feature work
takeaways: Technical debt is usually non-functional work such as refactoring, tests, docs, CI and deployment automation.
Only treat debt as a problem if it improves speed or quality of output or has an urgent cost of delay.
Classify each piece of work into one of four buckets: Functional Improvements, Program Work, Delivery Performance, or Unplanned Work.
Use a consistent vocabulary across planning levels to justify investing in debt fixes.
For work that does not fit a bucket, make small incremental improvements in every PR rather than big-bang projects.
summary.summary: This is a slide deck (Google Slides, view-only) from a talk by Ryan D, also published as a Medium article. It argues that teams don't need to halt feature delivery to address technical debt. The talk defines tech debt, gives examples such as removing globals, adding tests, improving docs, getting tests running in CI and automating deployments, and frames the challenge as communicating business value. It then presents an allocation framework that sorts work into four buckets and assigns them at each planning level, with guidance for unclassifiable work. The page text is mostly slide content with no code or measurements.
